prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on your case details and what you value (trial experience, record of big settlements, fee structure, communication style, language, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. Below are practical steps and criteria to identify a top Houston car-wreck lawyer, plus what to ask at a first meeting.

How to find a top Houston car-accident lawyer
- Use reputable directories and peer-review lists: Texas Bar Association referral service, Houston Bar Association, Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell (AV ratings), and client-review sites (Google, Yelp, Avvo).  
- Look for lawyers who focus on personal injury and specifically auto collisions (not general practitioners).  
- Prefer lawyers with trial experience and a track record of settlements/verdicts for similar injuries.  
- Check disciplinary history via the Texas Bar’s attorney lookup to confirm good standing.

Key qualifications to look for
- Years handling car-accident and injury cases in Texas.  
- Proven settlement/verdict history for injuries like yours (whiplash vs. catastrophic injuries vs. wrongful death).  
- Board certifications or peer-review ratings (e.g., AV Preeminent).  
- Familiarity with local courts, judges, and the major insurance companies in Texas.  
- Clear contingency-fee agreement (typical: no recovery, no fee) and transparent handling of expenses.

Questions to ask at a free initial consult
- How many car-accident cases have you handled, and how many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine (e.g., fractures, spinal cord, brain injury)? Can you share outcomes (settlement ranges or verdicts)?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (you or an associate/paralegal)?  
- What contingency fee percentage and who pays case expenses?  
- What is your communication policy and typical response time?  
- What is your assessment of my case and likely next steps?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific result or overly high-pressure promises.  
- Vague fee explanations or surprises about costs.  
- Poor client reviews mentioning missed deadlines or lack of communication.  
- No willingness to take the case to trial if needed.

What to bring to the first meeting
- Police report, photos of the crash/vehicle/damage, medical records and bills, employer records if lost wages, insurance information (yours and other drivers’), witness info, correspondence from insurance companies, and your notes on how the crash happened and injuries.

If you want, I can:
- Search and shortlist 3–5 highly rated Houston personal injury lawyers for car wrecks right now (I’ll need any preferences: language, trial vs. settlement focus, injury severity, etc.).  
- Provide a template list of questions you can print for consultations.

Which would you prefer? If you want a shortlist, tell me any preferences (severity of injury, ZIP code or area in Houston, language needs).
